core_obligations: Use the isomorphism of localisations to compare the two presentations, choosing for each generator a fraction expressing its image, and clear the finitely many denominators to obtain elements outside the primes with matching presentations (proof lines 31852-31864).
Apply the local isomorphism lemma to split the second algebra as a product so that inverting the idempotent of one factor gives the required isomorphism of localisations (proof lines 31865-31876).
proof_roadmap: Compare the presentations and clear denominators (proof lines 31851-31864).
Reduce to a product decomposition and conclude (proof lines 31865-31877).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that an isomorphism between the localisations of two finitely presented algebras at primes spreads out to an isomorphism after inverting a single element outside each prime (statement lines 31840-31849). The proof does not use a general limit argument: it compares the two explicit presentations, expresses the images of finitely many generators as fractions, clears the finitely many denominators to get the same algebra, and then reduces the remaining ambiguity by splitting off a factor (proof lines 31851-31877). Clearing denominators for the whole presentation at once is the step that carries the argument. H2.
